classification.difficultyReason: Use the Pythagorean identity to obtain a quadratic in sine, solve its two irrational roots and identify all four angles using reference angles and quadrants.

content.prompt: Solve $4\cos^2\theta+2\sin\theta=3$ for $0\leq\theta<360^\circ$ to the nearest degree.

answer.worked:
Using $\cos^2\theta=1-\sin^2\theta$:
$$\begin{align*}4(1-\sin^2\theta)+2\sin\theta&=3\\4-4\sin^2\theta+2\sin\theta&=3\\4\sin^2\theta-2\sin\theta-1&=0\\\sin\theta&=\frac{2\pm\sqrt{(-2)^2-4(4)(-1)}}{8}\\\sin\theta&=\frac{1\pm\sqrt5}{4}\end{align*}$$
For $\sin\theta=\dfrac{1+\sqrt5}{4}>0$, use quadrants 1 and 2:
$$\begin{align*}A&=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{1+\sqrt5}{4}\right)\\A&=54^\circ\\\theta&=54^\circ\text{ or }180^\circ-54^\circ\\\theta&=54^\circ\text{ or }126^\circ\end{align*}$$
For $\sin\theta=\dfrac{1-\sqrt5}{4}<0$, use the positive ratio for the reference angle and quadrants 3 and 4:
$$\begin{align*}A&=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{\sqrt5-1}{4}\right)\\A&=18^\circ\\\theta&=180^\circ+18^\circ\text{ or }360^\circ-18^\circ\\\theta&=198^\circ\text{ or }342^\circ\end{align*}$$
To the nearest degree, $\theta=54^\circ,126^\circ,198^\circ,342^\circ$.
